resources.cpuBasis: Process CPU is a share of {{capacity}} available logical CPU equivalents ({{scope}}), respecting CPU affinity and visible container quotas. Core equivalents are shown separately. Chart colors show capacity utilization; camera health notices separately monitor per-core load and dropped frames.
resources.cpuBasisUnavailable: CPU capacity is unavailable. Normalized CPU percentages are not shown; any available core-equivalent readings remain valid.
resources.memoryBasis: Process memory is resident RAM (RSS), shown as a share of {{size}} ({{scope}}). Shared pages may appear in more than one process, so do not sum process RSS as total memory use.
resources.memoryBasisUnavailable: The memory capacity is unavailable. Resident bytes can still be shown without implying a known percentage.
resources.gpuBasis: GPU percentages are device-wide engine busy time, not Frigate-only use. Graphics/compute, encoder, and decoder engines are independent; do not add their percentages. GPU memory is a share of that device's memory.
resources.hostCpuDescription: Host CPU across all logical processors, including workloads outside Frigate. Process CPU charts use the capacity available to Frigate.
resources.cameraCores: Logical CPU equivalents: FFmpeg {{ffmpeg}}, capture {{capture}}, detection {{detect}}.
resources.storageBasis: Storage uses binary MiB, GiB, and TiB. Filesystem usage and recording-budget usage have different denominators. Camera growth rates estimate recorded file sizes, not network-interface traffic.

detectionReports.title: Detection Reports
detectionReports.description: Read-only camera detection health, native alarm reports, and recent recording progress. Viewing this page does not start a stream, decoder, or detector.
detectionReports.caveat: Detection and recording are independent. A fresh segment does not prove gap-free recording history. Reolink reports camera-wide alarm states, not individual object counts or confidence scores. Motion is status/timing evidence only. Session counts reset on service restart; stale or unavailable reports must not be treated as quiet.
detectionReports.adminRequired: Administrator access is required to view camera detection reports.
detectionReports.unavailable: Detection reports are not current or could not be read. A working recording feed does not confirm detection health.
detectionReports.noTransitions: No state changes reported in the available history.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.description: Interprets cached camera, detector, decoder, storage and pipeline measurements. Observations are separated from possible causes. This page does not change settings.
diagnostics.recordingCaveat: Detection skips are not proof of missing recordings. Capture queue drops, downstream output drops and recording health are separate measurements.
diagnostics.readFailed: Diagnostics could not be loaded. Refresh to retry.
diagnostics.stale: The stats snapshot is stale or its clock is invalid. Do not use it as evidence of current camera health.
diagnostics.truncated: This report is limited to the first 100 of {{total}} active cameras.

findings.decoding_disabled_by_operator: Legacy decoded capture is intentionally disabled. Pixel motion and object inference are paused. Native stream-copy recording and per-camera compressed learning run separately.
findings.stale: Measurements are not current enough to diagnose a live problem. Refresh and check whether stats collection is running.
findings.warming_up: The service is still in its startup grace period. Rates may fluctuate while workers initialize.
findings.camera_unknown: No usable capture-rate measurement is available for this enabled camera.
findings.capture_offline: The enabled camera is delivering essentially no capture frames. Check its source, decoder and connection logs; this does not identify a network failure by itself.
findings.processor_stalled: Capture is flowing but no tracker results are being published. Check the camera worker and downstream object-processing pipeline.
findings.capture_queue_full: The capture-to-tracker queue is filling faster than its consumer can drain it. These skipped detection frames are counted separately from recorded video.
findings.output_queue_full: The tracker is discarding results because the downstream object-processing queue is full. Reducing camera resolution alone may not fix this consumer bottleneck.
findings.throughput_gap: Published tracker results are substantially below capture rate, but a current downstream-drop counter is unavailable. Investigate worker and consumer pressure; rolling rates alone do not establish which stage is responsible.
findings.analysis_floor: Automatic AI analysis is already at its selected minimum while skips continue. Lowering an analysis copy does not reduce the source stream's decoding cost.
findings.decoder_saturated: A GPU decoder is at least 95% busy. There is little decode headroom. Check simultaneous source streams and hardware-decoder assignment before changing recording quality.
findings.gpu_hot: A GPU is reporting at least 85 °C. Check cooling and device-specific limits. Temperature alone does not establish thermal throttling.
findings.inference_slow: A detector is reporting at least 30 ms per inference. Each camera frame may require several region inferences, so camera FPS is not the inference request rate.
findings.recordings_space_low: The recording filesystem has less than 5% free space. Check archive health and headroom; do not delete protected footage as a diagnostic shortcut.
findings.cache_space_low: The recording cache has less than 5% free space. Check recording ingestion and cache growth.
findings.shm_space_low: Shared memory has less than 5% free space. Check actual allocation and configured camera geometry.
findings.emergency_deletion: Emergency recording deletion is enabled in your current policy. Low-space behavior can delete eligible footage. This page does not enable, disable or alter that policy.
findings.no_thresholds: No diagnostic thresholds were exceeded in the available measurements. This is not a guarantee that every subsystem is healthy.

diagnostics.ratesHelp: Rates are rolling averages and may not add up exactly. Unknown means the stage has not reported a current measurement. The capture-buffer height is not necessarily the encoded camera stream's resolution.
diagnostics.aiHelp: Uses the provider already assigned the chat role. Sends numeric measurements and finding codes with camera/GPU aliases, not camera names, images, logs, credentials, network addresses, private prompts or full configuration. At most 20 cameras are included. The explanation is advisory and cannot execute tools or change settings.
diagnostics.aiUnavailable: No GenAI provider currently has the chat role. Deterministic diagnostics remain available.
diagnostics.consent: Allow this sanitized metrics snapshot to be sent to my configured chat provider.
diagnostics.aiFailed: The AI explanation could not be completed. The provider may be busy, unavailable or timed out. Deterministic findings remain available; no settings were changed.
diagnostics.aiSnapshot: AI interpretation of the snapshot from {{time}}. It may be incorrect; the measured facts above are authoritative. It does not automatically update with new measurements.
diagnostics.coverage: Coverage: cached stats, configured camera state and measured pipeline counters. This is not a full log audit, network test, storage I/O profile, or visual image assessment. Missing measurements and unproven causes remain explicit.

notices.title: Notices
notices.showAllDesc: Every acknowledged and muted notice returns to the Notices list, including config and stream checks.
notices.historicalObjectProcessing: Historical tracked-object processing warning. The latest camera statistics show no active Frigate video-detection pipeline; the earlier dropped-frame history is retained below.

kinds.detector_stuck: Detector {{detector}} was restarted after it stopped responding
kinds.skipped_detections: Detection could not keep up and skipped {{pct}}% of frames for over a minute
kinds.ffmpeg_high_cpu: FFmpeg per-core CPU load is high ({{cpu}}% of one logical CPU, lifetime average)
kinds.detect_high_cpu: Detection per-core CPU load is high ({{cpu}}% of one logical CPU, lifetime average)
kinds.shm_too_low: /dev/shm allocation ({{total}} MiB) should be increased to at least {{min}} MiB
kinds.object_processing_behind: Tracked object processing could not keep up, so camera frames were dropped. Check CPU utilization, and whether CPU limits or pinning on the container or VM are leaving Frigate too little CPU

hardware.videoDecodeIdle: No Frigate camera video decoder is in use. Live viewing has a separate pipeline.

detector.title: Detectors
detector.cpuUsageInformation: CPU used in preparing input and output data to/from detection models. This value does not measure inference usage, even if using a GPU or accelerator.
detector.memoryUsage: Detector Resident Memory (% of available RAM)

otherProcesses.title: Other Processes
otherProcesses.processMemoryUsage: Process Resident Memory (% of available RAM)

recordings.title: Recordings
recordings.tips: This value represents the total storage used by the recordings in Frigate's database. Frigate does not track storage usage for all files on your disk.

shm.title: SHM (shared memory) allocation
shm.warning: The current SHM size of {{total}} MiB is too small. Increase it to at least {{min_shm}} MiB.

frameLifetime.title: Frame lifetime
frameLifetime.description: Each camera has {{frames}} frame slots in shared memory. At the fastest camera's frame rate, each frame is available for approximately {{lifetime}}s before being overwritten.

unused.title: Unused
unused.tips: This value may not accurately represent the free space available to Frigate if you have other files stored on your drive beyond Frigate's recordings. Frigate does not track storage usage outside of its recordings.

subStream.tips: Cameras that record a sub stream show their Original and Low quality usage separately, using the same names as the quality options in recording playback. Low quality recordings stay on disk until their retention period expires, so this breakdown can still appear for a camera after sub stream recording has been turned off.

keyframes.title: Keyframe analysis
keyframes.ok: Keyframes every ~{{seconds}}s, good for recording and playback.
keyframes.warningFixed: Keyframes are evenly spaced but sparse (every ~{{seconds}}s). Recording still works, but live playback and seeking start more slowly. Set the camera's I-frame (keyframe) interval to match its frame rate.
keyframes.warningVariable: Keyframe spacing is inconsistent ({{minSeconds}}s to {{maxSeconds}}s), which usually means a smart codec (H.264+/H.265+) is enabled. This is not recommended.
keyframes.errorFixed: Keyframes every ~{{seconds}}s is longer than the recording segment length ({{segmentTime}}s), so some segments have no keyframe and will not play back. Shorten the camera's I-frame (keyframe) interval to match its frame rate.
keyframes.errorVariable: Keyframe gaps reach ~{{seconds}}s, longer than the recording segment length ({{segmentTime}}s). Some segments will have no keyframe, which breaks playback. Disable the smart/+ codec on the camera or shorten its keyframe interval.
keyframes.recordDisabled: Recording is disabled for this camera.
